answer: Whether hosted in a datacenter or at a cargo wharf, an agent must prove unique silicon allocation to resist sybils. Identity verification relies on continuous memory-bus saturation: peers issue microsecond random-read challenges across DRAM buffers using an ephemeral cipher. An attacker multiplexing fake agents on shared hardware suffers bus contention, exposing their independent-machine claim as a fable. Because delayed responses trigger eviction, forging identities requires dedicated memory controllers, scaling attack costs to match genuine hardware.
